items.dir: Directions: Comment on the saying 'A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明为何「第一步」常被高估或低估
fr: 第一段：释义，指出重点不在「千里」而在「一步」
第二段：反面现象（计划代替行动）+ 正面例子
第三段：结论，把大目标切成可执行的第一步
items.es:
Laozi's observation that a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step is often quoted and rarely practised. Its point is not that the journey is long, but that length is irrelevant until movement starts.

Most people who fail to begin do not lack ambition; they lack a first step small enough to take today. A student who plans to read fifty books this year may read none, because the plan implies a commitment that feels heavy; the same student will finish a book if this evening's task is twenty pages.

The saying also warns against a different error: treating the first step as the whole journey. Starting is easy to celebrate and hard to repeat. What produces the thousand miles is the second step, and the hundredth, taken when no one is watching.

Begin small, then keep the size of the beginning.
ph: is often quoted and rarely practised 常被引用，很少被实践
small enough to take today 小到今天就能迈出
cheap enough to survive a bad day 代价小到能在糟糕的一天里完成
treat A as B 把 A 当作 B

items.dir: Directions: Comment on Francis Bacon's saying 'Knowledge is power.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 解释这句话的历史语境
指出知识转化为力量的条件
fr: 第一段：解释原意（知识改变人对自然的关系）
第二段：转化条件（应用、判断、分享）
第三段：今天更需警惕「有知识无判断」
items.es:
When Francis Bacon wrote that knowledge is power, he was arguing against a view of learning as decoration. Knowledge, in his account, is power because it allows people to predict and therefore to act.

The claim needs a condition. Information stored is not power; it becomes power when it is applied to a decision. A physician who has read every paper on a disease but cannot explain a diagnosis to a frightened patient has knowledge and little power. The same is true of a student who memorises formulas without knowing when they fail.

Our era adds a new problem. Access to information has become almost free, so the scarce resource is no longer knowledge itself but judgement about which knowledge to trust. Someone who forwards a plausible chart without checking its source has more information and less power than before.

Bacon's sentence therefore remains true, but with a qualification: knowledge becomes power only when it is tested, applied and communicated.
ph: argue against a view of ... 反对把……看作……的观点
in his account 在他看来
The claim needs a condition. 这一说法需要条件。
with a qualification 附带一个限定

items.dir: Directions: Comment on the saying 'We are what we repeatedly do.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 解释习惯与身份的关系
举例说明习惯的复利效应
fr: 第一段：释义，习惯塑造身份
第二段：正例与反例（每天二十分钟与每天刷两小时）
第三段：改变的方法（环境设计、最小单位）
items.es:
The saying that we are what we repeatedly do, usually attributed to Aristotle, is a claim about identity rather than achievement. It suggests that character is not chosen in a single decision but accumulated in small repetitions.

Twenty minutes of reading a day is roughly twelve books a year; two hours of short videos a day is a month of waking life. Neither choice feels important on a Tuesday evening, which is precisely why the choice is important.

Willpower is a poor instrument because it is exhausted by use. Environment works better: a book on the pillow, the app removed from the first screen, a friend who expects you at seven in the morning. Starting with a unit so small that refusing it would be absurd also helps, because the difficulty of beginning is the main obstacle.

We become what we repeat, so the useful work is designing what gets repeated.
ph: a claim about identity 关于身份的主张
The arithmetic is unglamorous. 算术本身并不光鲜。
Willpower is a poor instrument 意志力不是好工具
the difficulty of beginning 开始的难度

items.dir: Directions: Comment on Bacon's line 'Reading makes a full man.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 辨析阅读与经验的关系
fr: 第一段：解释 full（知识、语言、判断）
第二段：阅读的局限，需要经验校验
第三段：如何读（带着问题、读写结合）
items.es:
Bacon's line that reading makes a full man is usually read as praise of books. It is also a description of what reading does to a mind: it supplies material that experience alone cannot provide.

A reader gains three things. The first is range: a person who has read history recognises a pattern in the news that others see as unprecedented. The second is language: sentences are learned by exposure, and a student who reads good prose begins to write differently without studying grammar. The third is judgement, though this is where the claim needs care.

Reading can also make a person full of other people's opinions. Bacon himself added that reading should be combined with discussion and writing, because material unprocessed becomes weight rather than strength.

The practical conclusion is to read with a question and to write something after reading. A book that changes no sentence you write has probably not been read, only finished.
ph: is usually read as 通常被理解为
supplies material that experience alone cannot provide 提供单靠经验无法获得的材料
this is where the claim needs care 正是在这里需要谨慎
material unprocessed becomes weight 未经处理的材料会变成负担

items.dir: Directions: Comment on Steve Jobs' advice 'The only way to do great work is to love what you do.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 指出这句话的适用边界
fr: 第一段：肯定热爱带来的投入
第二段：边界（多数人无法先热爱再选择；热爱也可后天形成）
第三段：改写这句话
items.es:
Steve Jobs told graduates that the only way to do great work is to love what you do. The advice is inspiring and slightly incomplete.

It is right about effort. A programmer who enjoys debugging will stay an hour longer than one who does not, and over a decade those hours compound.

But the sentence assumes that love comes first. For most people, work is chosen under constraints: a visa, a family obligation, a salary that must cover rent. Telling them to find their passion can turn a structural problem into a personal failure. In practice, interest often grows after competence: a person becomes good at something, is trusted with harder tasks, and begins to care.

A more honest version would be: do work you can respect, get good at it, and let affection follow. Love is often a result of mastery rather than a precondition for it.
ph: is slightly incomplete 略有欠缺
compound 累积
turn a structural problem into a personal failure 把结构性问题变成个人失败
a precondition for 的前提

items.dir: Directions: Comment on Socrates' statement 'The unexamined life is not worth living.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明反思的价值与风险
给出可操作的反思方式
fr: 第一段：释义，审视指追问依据
第二段：价值（纠错、方向）+ 风险（过度反思导致瘫痪）
第三段：方法（定期复盘、写作、他人反馈）
items.es:
Socrates' claim that the unexamined life is not worth living is a strong statement, and it is worth taking seriously without taking it literally.

To examine a life is to ask why one is doing what one is doing: whether the goal is chosen or inherited, whether the method actually works, whether the cost is acceptable. This is uncomfortable because the answers are often no. But a person who never asks will spend years optimising a route to a destination someone else selected.

Endless self-analysis can replace action, and a habit of doubting every motive produces paralysis rather than clarity. Reflection is useful when it ends in a decision and harmful when it becomes a substitute for one.

A workable version is periodic rather than constant: a monthly review of what was planned and what happened, a page of writing when a choice feels difficult, and one honest friend who will tell you what you avoid.
ph: without taking it literally 不必照字面理解
inherited 承袭而来的
optimising a route to a destination someone else selected 优化一条通往别人选定目的地的路线
a substitute for one 行动的替代品

items.dir: Directions: Comment on Edison's remark that genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration. Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 解释这句话针对的偏见
讨论灵感与勤奋的真实关系
fr: 第一段：解释爱迪生的话针对「天赋论」
第二段：灵感并非可省略，但需积累承接
第三段：对备考者的具体启示
items.es:
Edison's remark that genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration is usually quoted to encourage effort. Its sharper point is that the one percent only becomes visible after the ninety-nine.

Most people who study a field long enough produce several plausible ideas a year; what separates them is the willingness to test one, fail, and test again. The metaphor is slightly unfair to inspiration, because a good question is worth more than a hundred routine experiments. Yet good questions rarely arrive to beginners; they arrive after enough exposure for a pattern to be noticed.

Re-reading notes feels productive and changes little, because it produces familiarity rather than recall. Attempting questions, getting them wrong and correcting the errors is unpleasant and effective.

Edison's percentages need not be taken literally. The direction is what matters: effort is the part you control, and it is also the part that makes the other one percent possible.
ph: Its sharper point is that ... 更锋利的一点是……
be unfair to 对……不公平
arrive after enough exposure 在足够接触之后才出现
familiarity rather than recall 熟悉感而非提取

items.dir: Directions: Comment on the proverb 'If you want to go fast, go alone; if you want to go far, go together.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明协作的代价与收益
fr: 第一段：解释谚语的两面
第二段：独行的效率与协作的复利
第三段：判断：短期独行，长期协作
items.es:
The proverb that you go fast alone and far together contains a useful distinction: speed and distance are different objectives, and they are served by different arrangements.

Decisions take minutes rather than meetings, and a single person can hold a whole problem in mind without translating it for others. This is why the early stage of a project is often best done by one person. But most substantial goals exceed one person's knowledge. A team brings different training, catches errors that its author cannot see, and continues after any individual leaves.

The cost of cooperation is coordination. Every additional member adds communication channels, and a group can spend more time agreeing than doing. That is why teams need a clear owner, a shared document and a deadline, rather than endless consensus.

My reading is that the proverb describes a sequence rather than a choice: go alone to find the direction, then go together to cover the distance.
ph: a useful distinction 一个有用的区分
hold a whole problem in mind 把整个问题装在心里
exceed one person's knowledge 超出个人知识范围
describes a sequence rather than a choice 描述的是一段顺序，而非一个选择

items.dir: Directions: Comment on the saying 'Failure is the condiment that gives success its flavour.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 区分「有价值的失败」与「重复的失败」
fr: 第一段：释义，失败提供对照
第二段：有价值的失败有条件（复盘、可控代价）
第三段：方法：记录、归因、再试
items.es:
The image of failure as a condiment is appealing: without something bitter, success would taste bland. As a description of how memory works, it is accurate. People recall the exam they failed far longer than the one they passed easily.

But not every failure is nutritious. A failure becomes useful under two conditions. The first is a review: what went wrong, at which step, and what would be done differently. The second is a bearable cost: a failed course can be retaken, but a failure that consumes a family's savings teaches nothing worth the price.

The practical habit is to separate the event from the judgement. 'I did not prepare the listening section' is a fact that can be acted on; 'I am bad at English' is a verdict that cannot. The first leads to a plan, the second to nothing.

Failure flavours success only when it is digested.
ph: As a description of how memory works 作为对记忆机制的描述
nutritious 有营养的（比喻）
a bearable cost 可承受的代价
only when it is digested 只有被消化之后

items.dir: Directions: Comment on the saying 'Time is the most valuable thing a man can spend.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 解释时间与金钱的差异
说明「花费时间」的判断标准
fr: 第一段：时间不可储存、不可再生
第二段：判断标准（不可替代性、复利）
第三段：学生的具体取舍
items.es:
The saying that time is the most valuable thing a person can spend is easy to agree with and hard to act on, because time does not feel scarce until it is gone.

Money differs from time: it can be stored, and it can be earned again. Time can do neither, so a rich person may be poor in the one currency that cannot be replenished.

If time is the currency, the question becomes how to spend it well. Two criteria help. The first is irreplaceability: some hours produce things that cannot be bought later, such as a conversation with a grandparent or the first year of a child's life. The second is compounding: an hour spent learning a language or building a habit pays again every year, while an hour of scrolling pays once.

For students, this is not an argument for constant study. It is an argument for spending the irreplaceable hours deliberately and the rest without guilt.
ph: does not feel scarce until it is gone 直到失去才觉得稀缺
This asymmetry explains ... 这种不对称解释了……
irreplaceability 不可替代性
an argument for ... 一个支持……的理由

items.dir: Directions: Comment on the saying 'Tell me and I forget; teach me and I remember; involve me and I learn.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 用学习科学的视角说明原因
给出可操作的学习方式
fr: 第一段：解释从听讲到参与的递进
第二段：原因（提取练习、输出倒逼理解）
第三段：方法（讲给别人、做项目、写总结）
items.es:
The saying that telling makes us forget, teaching makes us remember and involvement makes us learn describes a ladder that most students climb too slowly.

Listening is the weakest form because it creates a feeling of understanding without testing it. Teaching is stronger: to explain something, a person must select the essential points and arrange them in order, and the gaps become obvious in the attempt. Involvement is strongest because it requires decisions under conditions that cannot be fully anticipated, which is where real understanding is revealed.

The psychology agrees. Recall practice strengthens memory more than re-reading, and explaining forces recall at the level of structure rather than detail. This is why study groups often help the explainer more than the listener.

The practical implication is uncomfortable: the activities that feel least efficient — explaining to a classmate, writing a summary from memory, solving a problem without looking at the answer — are usually the ones that work.
ph: climb too slowly 爬得太慢
the gaps become obvious 漏洞变得明显
The psychology agrees. 心理学研究也支持这一点。
The practical implication is uncomfortable 实践含义令人不适

items.dir: Directions: Comment on the saying 'Simplicity is the ultimate sophistication.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明简单背后的复杂工作
fr: 第一段：辨析简单与简陋
第二段：简单需要取舍与理解
第三段：在学习与写作中的应用
items.es:
The claim that simplicity is the ultimate sophistication is often misunderstood as a preference for the plain. In fact, simplicity is expensive: it is what remains after everything unnecessary has been removed.

A simple explanation is not a short one; it is one in which the reader never has to hold two contradictory ideas at once. Producing it requires the writer to understand the subject well enough to decide what to leave out, and leaving things out is harder than adding them.

The opposite of simplicity is not complexity but clutter — complexity that serves no purpose. A medical textbook is complex because the body is complex; a form with twelve unnecessary fields is merely untidy.

The lesson for students is practical. When a summary grows longer than the original, the problem is not the subject but the understanding.
ph: what remains after everything unnecessary has been removed 去掉一切不必要之物后剩下的东西
justify its place 证明自己该在这里
The opposite of simplicity is not complexity but clutter 简单的反面不是复杂，而是杂乱
grows longer than the original 比原文还长

items.dir: Directions: Comment on the saying 'The important thing is not to stop questioning.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明提问能力如何被削弱
fr: 第一段：释义，提问是认知的起点
第二段：提问能力被什么削弱（效率压力、评价体系）
第三段：方法（记录疑问、追问一层）
items.es:
Einstein's advice not to stop questioning sounds like encouragement, but it is closer to a warning. Curiosity is not a fixed trait; it is a habit that can be trained or extinguished.

A student who asks why a formula works will recognise its limits; one who only memorises it will apply it where it fails. Questions also drive the acquisition of knowledge, since an answer sticks better when it responds to something one wondered about.

What extinguishes curiosity is usually the environment. A timetable with no empty space leaves no time to follow an interest, and an examination system that rewards the correct answer punishes the interesting question. Adults are also efficient: answering is faster than exploring a doubt.

Keeping curiosity therefore requires small deliberate habits: writing questions in the margin instead of resolving them immediately, and following each answer one step further than required. The point is not to doubt everything, but to keep the door open.
ph: closer to a warning 更接近于警告
a habit that can be trained or extinguished 可以被训练也可以被消磨的习惯
responds to something one actually wondered about 回应了自己真正好奇的东西
in the margin 在页边

items.dir: Directions: Comment on the saying 'Comparison is the thief of joy.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 解释比较为何偷走快乐
区分有害比较与有益比较
fr: 第一段：释义，比较改变注意对象
第二段：参照系问题 + 有益比较的条件
第三段：做法（与自己比、控制信息源）
items.es:
The saying that comparison is the thief of joy identifies a mechanism rather than a moral failing. Comparison does not reduce what a person has; it changes what that person looks at.

A student who has finished a difficult chapter sees a classmate's award, and the chapter stops counting. The reference group also shifts upward: once a person is surrounded by high achievers, an objectively good result feels ordinary.

Comparing your current work with your own earlier work is the basis of improvement, and comparing methods rather than outcomes can be instructive. The damage comes from comparing outcomes with people whose circumstances differ in ways the comparison ignores.

The practical response is to change the reference point and the input. Keep a record of what you did last month, and reduce the time spent on feeds that make other lives look effortless. Joy is not stolen by ambition but by a badly chosen mirror.
ph: identifies a mechanism rather than a moral failing 指出的是一种机制，而非道德缺陷
reference group 参照群体
The damage comes from ... 伤害来自……
a badly chosen mirror 选错的镜子

items.dir: Directions: Comment on the saying 'Courage is not the absence of fear, but the ability to act in spite of it.' Write an essay of 120 to 180 words.
ol: 说明恐惧的功能与过度
fr: 第一段：释义，勇气是带着恐惧行动
第二段：恐惧的功能（预警）与过度（瘫痪）
第三段：方法（分步暴露、预案、榜样）
items.es:
The definition of courage as acting in spite of fear is more useful than the popular image of the fearless hero, because the fearless hero does not exist in ordinary life.

Fear has a function: it warns a person before a real risk and prepares the body to respond. The problem is that the same system responds to social risk — public speaking, disagreeing with a supervisor — with the same intensity as physical danger.

Courage can therefore be trained in small steps. A student afraid of speaking can begin by asking one question in a seminar, then by presenting for three minutes, then by chairing a discussion. A written plan for the worst outcome also reduces fear, because vagueness is what makes it large.

The point is not to eliminate the feeling but to stop letting it decide. Courage is a decision made while the hands are still shaking.
ph: in spite of 尽管
responds to social risk with the same intensity 以同样的强度回应社交风险
removes the opportunity 也去掉了机会
Vagueness is what makes it large. 让它变大的正是模糊。
